To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed nearest-neighbour search algorithms for constrained Delauney triangulation models of line features are efficient in terms of computational time and memory requirements, and that the algorithms are robust in terms of the number of distance calculations needed to determine nearest-neighbours.

constrained Delauney triangulation is a good model to represent linear objects in a GIS and that the proposed nearest-neighbour search procedure is an efficient method to find the nearest edge to a query point.

(i) the nearest neighbour of a line feature can be found by searching along the edges of the feature, and (ii) the nearest neighbour to an arbitrary point can be found by a search along a set of edges emanating from the point.

the development of efficient and robust methods for the computation of proximity relationships within triangulated spatial data structures.
developing efficient and robust methods for proximity search with spatial models.

constrained Delaunays provide an efficient means of searching for nearest neighbours in spatial databases, and that the search procedures presented here are suitable for use in such databases, especially in applications where the spatial data are represented as a triangulated model.
